scoring_justification: Full recompute from raw DFT output infeasible because agent only provides final values; T1/T2 not feasible. We use result-level comparison to the paper's I‑rich formation energies and defect levels with tolerances, relying on honest DFT execution.

outputs.description: Defect formation energies under I-rich conditions. The checker compares each value to the paper-reported formation energies with an appropriate tolerance.

Defect level positions for I_i on flat and vacant terminations, with VBM and CBM references. The checker compares these values to the paper-reported defect levels and band edges with an appropriate tolerance.

output_contract.notes: The task focuses only on the I-rich chemical condition, as that supports the main claim of I_i being the dominant carrier-trapping defect. Charge density visualizations and other chemical conditions are omitted per scope. The formation energies from Table 1 and defect levels from Figure 2 of the source paper serve as hidden targets; the agent must re-compute them from first principles.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold formation energies (I‑rich, from paper Table 1) and defect levels (from Figure 2).
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Table 1 (I‑rich column) and Figure 2 defect level diagram.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted directly from the paper's published values; the same numbers are used by the reference solver solve.sh.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact quantities the paper reports for the same defects and chemical condition; they serve as the hidden reference for result-level comparison.

steps.description: Compare each submitted formation energy to the paper's I‑rich gold with tolerance 0.05 eV. Score per defect as max(0,1 - |delta|/0.05), then average.
Compare submitted I_i defect levels and band edges to the paper gold (level ~0.65 eV, VBM=0.0, CBM~1.55 eV) with tolerance 0.1 eV (0.02 eV for VBM). Score similarly, averaged over rows.
